Optimal.Notes: Full quality settings at native resolution with a stable 60 fps lock — this is the sweet spot for Geometry Dash on Deck. The game is light enough that high settings cost almost nothing extra over low settings.

profiles.Summary: Geometry Dash is an extremely lightweight 2D rhythm-based platformer that runs natively well within the Steam Deck's capabilities, easily hitting 60 fps at full resolution with minimal GPU and CPU load. The game's ProtonDB platinum rating confirms it runs smoothly under Proton with no major compatibility issues.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's extremely modest PC requirements (OpenGL 2.0, 512 MB RAM), its 2D nature, and the Deck's hardware capabilities. On first run, verify that audio is in sync with the rhythm — if it isn't, try switching to Proton Experimental or a GE-Proton build.

MaxBattery.Notes: This 2D game is so lightweight that even a 4 W TDP and a low GPU clock easily sustain a locked 60 fps. The battery savings here are dramatic without any visible quality loss for a game of this style.

KnownIssues: Controller/gamepad input may require some configuration as the game only has partial controller support — keyboard bindings may feel more natural.
The game uses OpenGL, which works fine under Proton but may occasionally require a specific Proton version if issues arise.
Music sync is critical to gameplay; if audio latency issues appear, try switching Proton versions.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With FPS Bypass enabled the game can render above 60 fps internally, but the LCD display caps output at 60 Hz; this profile lets the hardware run unconstrained for the smoothest possible frame pacing. TDP is uncapped but the game will rarely pull more than 6-8 W anyway.

Optimal.Notes: Full visuals at native resolution with Smooth Fix enabled for proper frame pacing — the game looks and plays as intended. 60 fps is rock-solid at this TDP, and battery life remains excellent for a handheld session.

profiles.Summary: Geometry Dash is an extremely lightweight 2D rhythm-based platformer from 2014 with minimal GPU requirements, making it effortless for the Steam Deck to run at full speed. The game targets 60 fps natively and the Deck can sustain this well within a very low TDP envelope, leaving plenty of headroom for long battery life.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very modest 2014 PC minimum requirements (OpenGL 2.0, 512 MB RAM) and the Steam Deck hardware. On your first run, verify that music and visuals stay in sync and check that the FPS counter (Show FPS) reads a stable 60 or 90 — if it does, you can confidently drop TDP further.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 4 W TDP and a reduced GPU clock, Geometry Dash runs effortlessly at 60 fps — it is a 2D game with very low GPU demands. Low Detail Mode and particles off shave a little extra power for maximum session length.

KnownIssues: Partial controller support means some menus may be easier to navigate with touch or the trackpad rather than buttons.
The game uses OpenGL, which runs through Proton's translation layer — occasional minor stutters on first shader compile are possible.
Music sync is critical in a rhythm game; any frame pacing issues can affect feel, so a stable 60 fps cap is strongly recommended over uncapped.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The OLED's 90 Hz refresh pairs well with the game's uncapped renderer for the smoothest possible feel — Geometry Dash is light enough to sustain well above 90 fps without breaking a sweat. Note that the in-game FPS Limit must be set to 0 (or disabled) to allow the frame rate to exceed 60.
